body:
Adding {forceOptimisticNavigation: true} to the router.push call fixed it.

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/48642
Shameless plug: [vite-plugin-ssr](https://vite-plugin-ssr.com) just added support for Tauri. Example: [vite-plugin-ssr.com/tauri](https://vite-plugin-ssr.com/tauri).

Hey @Royceb would you re-open this issue?  

Adding `forceOptimisticNavigation` is a temporary fix that degrades the user experience by forcing hard navigation.

See https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/48642#issuecomment-1517477699

Doesn't look like you can build any reasonable application using NextJS and Tauri. You can't have dynamic routes like `/posts/1`. Not even search params work, eg. `posts?postId=1`.

Dynamic route issue: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/48022

looks like I am moving to Vite 🎉

I've run into the same problem when using the Next.js app router. It seems to affect any kind of route navigation – I created another simple repro here:

https://github.com/reupen/tauri-nextjs-repro

This only happens in (release or debug) builds and not in dev mode (where the Next.js dev server is used).

What happens is that the Next.js .txt metadata file for the route navigated to ends up being opened as a web page. So, in my example, `subpage.txt` is opened in the browser.

I noticed (in a debug build) that the content type of the .txt file is reported as `text/html` in the developer tools, rather than `text/plain`. Not sure if that's the cause of the problem (or just a red herring).

There's no problem when using another server to serve the static files and opening the site in a normal web browser. I'm on Ubuntu 22.04.

I did some further investigation. The issue is related to content types, though not in the way I expected. Here, when the web page loads, Next.js checks if the `content-type` header in the `fetch()` response for the `.txt` file (`tauri://localhost/subpage.txt` in my example) starts with `text/plain`:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/38d9d2efee50e785f9fc707a9fcb349e49fa6dd5/packages/next/src/client/components/router-reducer/fetch-server-response.ts#L78-L93

However, the `content-type` header is not set. In fact, there don't appear to be any headers set in the response at all. This causes Next.js to decide to navigate to the `.txt` file instead when the route is actually navigated to.

I confirmed that to be the case by patching that line of code in Next.js to skip the content type check.

Is there any particular reason why no response headers would be set in the response returned by `fetch()` in the browser?

Thanks

issue.title: Tauri + NextJS app directory using router.push from next/navigation doesn't render page correctly

labels.name: Linking and Navigating
labels.description: Related to Next.js linking (e.g., <Link>) and navigation.

issue.body: ### Verify canary release - [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.1.0: Sun Oct 9 20:15:09 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8792.41.9~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 Binaries: Node: 18.12.1 npm: 8.19.2 Yarn: 1.22.19 pnpm: 7.24.2 Relevant packages: next: 13.3.1-canary.16 eslint-config-next: 13.3.0 react: 18.2.0 react-dom: 18.2.0 ``` ### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure) App directory (appDir: true), Routing (next/router, next/navigation, next/link), Static HTML Export (output: "export") ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/Royceb/nextjs-app-dir-tauri-router-push-example ### To Reproduce 1. Ran `npx create-next-app@latest --experimental-app` 2. Set up Tauri 2.1: Ran `pnpm add -D @tauri-apps/cli` 2.2: Added `tauri` to package.json scripts. Ran `pnpm tauri init`. 3. Updated next.config.js to use `output: "export"` for SSG (Static Generation). 4. Made a simple page at `app/examplePage/page.tsx` 5. Imported `next/navigation` in `app/page.tsx` and added a button that calls `router.push('/examplePage')`. 6. Ran `pnpm tauri dev` and clicked the button. The app navigated to the example page as expected and rendered it properly. 7. Ran `pnpm tauri build` and opened the app. Clicked the button. The app did naviate to the example page, but it did not render it properly. The page rendered code as text instead of rendering the page. ### Describe the Bug I was uncertain whether to open this in Tauri or NextJS, so I opened issues in both platforms. While utilizing a NextJS application, version 13, and the experimental app directory, I encountered an issue where using router.push to navigate to a new page fails to render correctly. Although the navigation occurs successfully, the page only displays code as text instead of rendering the expected content. I have not found any console logs or errors related to this issue. This problem only arises after building and running the application. Locally, everything seems to be functioning correctly. Recording: https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3469263/233444738-73f955e9-2aae-43fb-a92b-d0a4c1dd3c3e.mov Screenshot: ### Expected Behavior The page should render correctly. ### Which browser are you using? (if relevant) _No response_ ### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant) _No response_

body:
@reupen Are you also on macOS? Or on Linux? In case you're on Linux, can you add the `"linux-headers"` feature flag to the tauri dependency in Cargo.toml and try again?

Anyway, even if that brings back the headers, Tauri's "server" will fallback to an html mime type for txt files: https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/5fdf8dcb8ed171d06121dceb32078a7e4f86cc64/core/tauri-utils/src/mime_type.rs#L48-L86. Looks more like an oversight to me since text/plain should be the fallback for textual files according to mdn

@FabianLars I'm on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04). Did you mean the `linux-protocol-headers` feature? Can confirm that `linux-protocol-headers` + patching that bit of Tauri's code fixes the problem :tada: 

(I actually first tried patching that before I started digging into what was happening in Next.js...)
whoops, yeah that flag. i had Wry's flag in mind, sorry 😅
